descriptionChirho: Qal active participle: one who nurtures, carries, or rears a child — a nurse, guardian, or foster-parent; confirmed by Arabic مُرَبِّي / مُرَبِّيَة 'rearer/nurturer', Korean 양육자 / 유모 'caregiver/nurse', Swahili mlezi/walezi 'caretaker(s)', Hindi पालक / धाई 'guardian/nurse'.

Qal passive participle and Niphal passive: those who have been reared, nursed, or carried — the passive counterpart of the nurturing sense; Arabic الْمُرَبَّوْنَ 'those reared', تُحْمَلْنَ 'be carried'; Korean 기른 자들 'those raised', 안길 것이다 'will be held'; Swahili waliolelewa 'those who were brought up', watanyonyeshwa 'they will be nursed'.

Niphal participle (adjectival) and adjective forms: faithful, trustworthy, reliable, sure, enduring — describing a person or thing as dependable; Arabic أَمِينٌ / أُمَنَاء 'faithful/trustworthy', Korean 신실한 'faithful', Swahili mwaminifu/waaminifu 'faithful/trustworthy', Hindi विश्वासयोग्य / विश्वसनीय 'trustworthy'.

Niphal finite verb (imperfect, perfect with conjunction): to be confirmed, established, verified, made firm — an eventive sense distinct from the stative participle; Arabic يَثْبُتْ / تَثبُتُوا (root ث-ب-ت 'be firm') and يُصَدَّقْ (root ص-د-ق 'be verified'), Korean 이루어지다 / 굳건하게 하다 'be fulfilled/made firm', Swahili -thibitika / -imarishwa 'be confirmed/strengthened', Hindi स्थिर हो / दृढ़ रहो 'become firm/stable'.

Hifil: to believe, give credence to, accept as true — cognitive assent to a message, person, or divine promise; Arabic آمَنَ / يُؤْمِنُ (root ء-م-ن 'believe') and يُصَدِّقُ (root ص-د-ق 'credit as true'), Korean 믿다 'believe', Swahili -amini 'believe', Hindi विश्वास करना 'believe'.

Hifil with 'trust/rely' semantics: to place confidence in, depend on — distinct from mere belief by implying reliance and personal confidence; Arabic يَثِقُ / تَثِقْ (root و-ث-ق 'trust/rely') and تَأْمَنُ 'feel secure about', Korean 신뢰하다 'trust/rely on', Hindi भरोसा करना 'trust/rely on', Swahili -amini / -tegemea 'trust/rely on'.
